note: Template series kit for series_card.py. Copy it into the author's private project and adapt the wording; keep the keys. Archetypes follow the Ink Theater method of OpenMontage.

formats.label: Visual explanation
formats.visual_brief: Show the phenomenon first, then the mechanism. Turn the idea into one physical action on a simple object performed by the hero; explain with labels and arrows on the object at the moment it changes.
event_patterns: before → action → after of one object
dramaturgy: a naive attempt partly works and breaks
connect with but/therefore, not and then
1–2 s of quiet after the insight

formats.label: Author monologue
formats.visual_brief: The hero does something with an object while speaking, and the thought changes the action. Camera address is brief; most time goes to hands, object, reaction and pause.
event_patterns: an action that embodies the thought
an object that argues with the hero

formats.label: Staged dialogue
formats.visual_brief: A conversation as a scene of actions: each line is answered by a deed, each move complicates the situation, the author keeps the last turn. A second character stays silent and acts, or has its own voice; the speaker's mouth stays hidden without verified lip-sync.
event_patterns: the other one does what the hero feared

formats.label: Thought experiment
formats.visual_brief: The assumption as a deed in a lived-in world: every changed condition is a new physical consequence on screen, performed by the hero on an object. Label it as a thought experiment; state the model's limit in one line near the end. No 'A = B' cards.
event_patterns: the assumption works and has an unexpected consequence
one condition changes and the world behaves differently
logic pushed to absurdity by a deed

styles.photoreal: live scene in a world from worlds.json
styles.ink: Ink Theater: black line on white paper, a mascot performs the action on a simple contraption; black = structure and hero, orange = flow and arrows only, red = the problem, blue = the good end state; ≥35% empty paper; a programmatic clip rendered locally and inserted into Vids
styles.screen: a plausible interface filling the frame, labelled as an example, with an on-screen event
styles.overlay: up to 3 words over the shot, tied to the object at the moment of change

archetypes.mechanism: load → crank → the contraption works → the result pops out
archetypes.journey_pitfalls: a path draws on, the hero walks, falls into a pit or hits a node
archetypes.one_to_many: one source splits into branches that each act
archetypes.push_uphill: slow strained push up, the crest, a fast roll back
archetypes.well_extract: lower a bucket into noise and pull out the one valuable thing
archetypes.two_attempts: fails, then works; the difference is visible

shot_sizes.insert: insert: a screen or object filling the frame
